profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: THE WHOLE BAG IS IN A FIGHT
profiles.profile: This is a full-scale plumbing disaster with a couple of shiny faucet handles. The driver has had moments, but the irons keep sawing the floor out from under him and the short game usually shows up wearing work boots and no plan. What makes it weird is the occasional burst where the putter or scrambling grabs the wheel for a minute, then the ball-striking tackles him again like it’s personal. The profile is stable in the worst possible way: lots of damage, very little rescue, and just enough random competence to keep the hope alive before the next faceplant.

profiles.name: graycrum
profiles.profile: This guy lives in the ugly little gap between “make enough saves” and “stop nuking approach shots.” The short game is the calling card, and when the wedges are cooking he can absolutely drag a round back from the dead. The annoying part is that the tee ball and irons keep taking turns tripping over themselves, so the good stuff usually has to work overtime. There’s a real mixed bag here: some rounds look sneaky solid, others look like the yardage book got hit by a truck. Still, the rescue tools are real, which is why he keeps hanging around instead of bleeding out completely.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.profile: This is a brutal little repeatable story: the tee game and irons are staging a coup against the rest of the card, and nobody’s winning that civil war. The putter hasn’t been nearly loud enough to cover for the amount of smoke coming off the long game, and the short game is usually too busy getting dragged into the mess. There are a couple of isolated scraps where something looked playable, but the overall file is pure survival horror. When the ball goes missing, it doesn’t just miss by a little — it goes straight into the woods and fills out paperwork.
